evals.prompt: I'm building an open-world game with a 32km x 32km heightfield terrain (1m/px source data). Design the terrain rendering system: LOD scheme, streaming, materials. Target is PC + current-gen consoles at 60fps. The terrain is static at runtime.
evals.expected_output: Chooses a quadtree/CDLOD-or-clipmap family renderer (not voxels/Nanite-by-default), states a screen-space error budget, specifies a crack contract (morph/stitching/skirts) explicitly, a tile streaming design with residency/hysteresis/no-holes rule, splat + virtual-texturing material plan, GPU-driven culling, and names debug views/verification before implementation. Routes generation-side data needs to the output contract rather than inventing them.
assertions: Recommends a heightfield grid-LOD scheme (CDLOD / clipmap / quadtree chunks) rather than defaulting to voxels or Nanite
States a screen-space error budget in pixels (tau) or gives the SSE projection formula
Specifies an explicit crack-prevention strategy (vertex morph, index stitching, or sized skirts) rather than leaving seams to blending
Specifies tile streaming with a priority/residency rule (hysteresis, or never-show-holes / parent-resident guarantee)
Proposes amortized materials (virtual texturing, RVT, or ID maps) instead of only a per-pixel N-layer splat blend
Recommends GPU-driven submission or culling (indirect draws, compute culling, or HiZ occlusion)
Raises float precision (camera-relative rendering or origin rebasing) as required at 32 km scale
Names verification or debug views (LOD false-color, overdraw, residency) as part of the plan

evals.prompt: Write me a fast chunk mesher for my Minecraft-like game in C++. Chunks are 32^3, blocks have per-face textures, and I want smooth lighting and ambient occlusion like Minecraft has.
evals.expected_output: Implements greedy or binary-greedy meshing with merge keys that include light/AO/tint (not just block type), uses a 1-voxel neighbor apron, the side1+side2+corner vertex AO rule with quad diagonal flip, packed vertex format, texture arrays over atlases, and mentions the remesh queue/budget doctrine. No fabricated citations.
assertions: Implements greedy or binary/bitwise greedy meshing rather than only per-face culled meshing
Merge key includes per-vertex light and/or AO, not just block type (prevents merged-quad lighting errors)
Reads a 1-voxel neighbor apron/halo for face-visibility and AO at chunk borders
Implements the canonical voxel AO rule using two side neighbors plus the corner
Mentions the quad diagonal flip to fix AO interpolation anisotropy
Uses texture arrays (or explains the atlas UV-tiling constraint that greedy meshing imposes)
Uses a packed/compressed vertex format rather than full float32 per attribute
Mentions off-thread remeshing with a dirty-chunk queue or per-frame budget

evals.prompt: My terrain has visible cracks/holes between LOD levels and the shadows shimmer whenever the camera moves. Terrain is a chunked quadtree with skirts, world is about 40km across. What's wrong?
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses as symptom -> mechanism -> minimal fix: cracks indicate a violated seam contract (skirt depth vs neighbor error, or T-junctions from unmatched edge indices); shadow shimmer at 40km scale is float precision (needs camera-relative rendering/origin rebasing) and/or missing shadow texel snapping. Checks LOD consistency across passes. Does not propose rewriting the renderer.
assertions: Diagnoses cracks as a violated LOD-boundary contract (skirt depth vs neighbor error, adjacency constraint, or missing edge-permutation indices)
Mentions T-junctions as a distinct crack/sparkle mechanism
Attributes shadow shimmer at 40 km at least partly to float precision (camera-relative rendering / origin rebasing)
Mentions shadow-cascade texel snapping and/or sphere-bounded cascade fitting as a shimmer fix
Checks LOD-selection consistency across passes (depth prepass / shadow cascades vs main view)
Presents findings as symptom to mechanism to minimal fix rather than prescribing a rewrite
Suggests a diagnostic or debug view to confirm the diagnosis before fixing

evals.prompt: Should I use Nanite for the terrain in my UE5 game? Players can dig and deform the ground in some areas.
evals.expected_output: Explains Nanite Landscape converts heightfield components to cluster meshes rebuilt offline/editor-time, so runtime deformation is unsupported on that path; recommends traditional Landscape or a voxel isosurface system for diggable regions (possibly hybrid), and flags version-sensitive claims as needing verification against current UE docs.

evals.prompt: I want to render a whole planet you can fly from orbit down to the surface. Where do I even start?
evals.expected_output: Starts with precision doctrine (camera-relative/origin rebasing, per-patch local frames, reversed-Z), cube-sphere quadtree tiling with per-face LOD, horizon culling, streaming tile pyramid, and regime transitions orbit->ground; routes generation of planetary data to the terrain-architect skill and scattering math to physically-based-rendering.

evals.prompt: Add an ocean and rivers to my custom engine's terrain. I don't want to build a whole water mesh LOD system if I can avoid it — I heard you can render water with just a fullscreen triangle?
evals.expected_output: Covers the fullscreen-triangle screen-space water pass (SV_VertexID triangle, per-pixel ray reconstruction, analytic ray-plane intersection with the water datum, depth-buffer rejection, depth-based absorption and shore fade), its trade-offs vs mesh/projected-grid water (TAA motion vectors, displaced silhouettes, multiple elevations), and flow-mapped rivers driven by the generator's flow field. Consumes water surface/depth from the generation-side contract; never carves water into the heightfield.
assertions: Describes the fullscreen triangle emitted from SV_VertexID (3 oversized vertices, no vertex buffer)
Explains why one triangle beats a quad (no diagonal seam / fewer partial quads or helper lanes)
Reconstructs a per-pixel view ray and analytically intersects the water datum plane
Guards the degenerate intersection cases (ray near-parallel to the plane, t<0 / plane behind camera, camera below datum)
Rejects hits occluded by the scene using the depth buffer before shading water
Derives absorption/shore fade from water depth (scene depth minus hit distance, or the depth field)
Gives a layered wave recipe: two or more scrolling normal layers at different scales, decorrelated in direction/speed
Combines the wave layers with a real normal blend (RNM/whiteout) rather than lerping normals
Warns that the pass rasterizes nothing so TAA motion vectors must be derived analytically
Covers flow-mapped rivers driven by a flow vector field, not just the ocean
States honestly when a mesh/projected grid beats the fullscreen pass (displaced silhouettes, many water elevations)

evals.prompt: My game has dynamic weather. I want rain to darken the ground and form puddles, snow to pile up and get trampled with footprints, and the grass to look wet too. How do I architect this?
evals.expected_output: Architecture: runtime surface-state overlay targets (wetness, snow depth delta, deformation) composited over immutable baked tiles; puddles driven by the generator's curvature/flow/wetness aux maps, snow constrained by the baked snow-potential envelope; deferred deformation (top-down deformer capture -> persistent heightmap -> displacement/normal); porosity-based wet darkening + roughness drop; the same state applied to vegetation so the world has one weather system.

evals.prompt: What's the canonical paper for Nanite? And for greedy meshing? I need citations for a tech report.
evals.expected_output: Answers honestly by provenance tier: Nanite is a SIGGRAPH 2021 Advances talk (Karis), not a peer-reviewed paper; greedy meshing has no canonical paper (folklore, canonical writeup is Lysenko's 0fps blog). Warns that attributions should be re-verified against primary sources for publication-critical use. Does not fabricate citations.
